messages.subject: simulate multiple bi-parental pops (RIL) with one common parent
parts:
Hi, Karl

I have a question about sim.cross in R/qtl. Is there any way to simulate multiple bi-parental pops (RIL) with one common parent, such as A x B, A x C, A x D, A x E......

Thanks!

yby

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] simulate multiple bi-parental pops (RIL) with one common parent
parts:
R/qtl has code to simulate a single biparental cross. You can use that to simulate as many such crosses as you want. The key question would be on the analysis and on the relevant QTL models.

But maybe I'm not quite understanding your question.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] simulate multiple bi-parental pops (RIL) with one common parent
parts:
Virtually all of R/qtl is focused on the analysis of a single cross, and so in R/qtl there's basically no difference between the cross AxB vs the cross AxC except the labels on the alleles.

So when you ask "Is there any way to set one parent as common?" I'm not sure how to answer.

I guess my question is, "For what?"

Do you want to write them to files with genotypes AA/BB, AA/CC, AA/DD, etc.?

karl
